title: Customer Rescue Lane & Contracted Acceptance Protocol
creator: Elena Park
description:
Problem: Strategic customers occasionally trigger emergency escalation requests that require fast delivery or configuration changes outside normal roadmap lanes. Today we lack a formal, contract-linked process that defines scope, acceptance criteria, and guaranteed rescue windows for 'top account' escalations. This causes ad-hoc firefighting, unclear promises to customers, and a lack of measurable SLA-backed outcomes.

Goal: Create a lightweight but auditable 'Rescue Lane' and a Contracted Acceptance Protocol that productizes emergency intake for top accounts: (1) standardized eligibility and intake checklist; (2) timeboxed rescue lanes (T+X business days) with clear scope and rollback rules; (3) acceptance criteria tied to contract-level outcomes; (4) automated routing to Dedicated/Private ops and an engineer rotation; (5) dashboarding and post-rescue retro workflow to capture regressions and cost.

Success metrics: number of escalations handled within promised window, time to first meaningful response, % of rescues meeting acceptance criteria, NPS delta for accounts using Rescue Lane, and total cost of escalations as percent of revenue for enrolled customers.
acceptance_criteria: A documented intake checklist exists and is published to Confluence for CS/Account teams
Contracts can opt-in to Rescue Lane and generate a unique intake token that maps to SLO and cost bracket
Routing rules created: urgent production-impact -> on-call eng rotation + Dedicated ops; non-urgent -> prioritized backlog lane
90% of intake requests acknowledged within 2 business hours in pilot cohort
Acceptance criteria templates for common rescue types (performance regression, data isolation issue, config rollback) available and used in 75% of pilot cases
Dashboard tile shows current active rescues, age, owner, and outcome status
Post-rescue retro template completed for each closed rescue and surfaced into roadmap triage if a product fix is required

decisions: Pilot will use opt-in contract addendum rather than being auto-applied to all enterprise customers
Rescue windows for pilot will be 48 hours (critical) and 5 business days (high/major), adjustable after metrics review
Charge model for pilot: use internal credits to invoice zero $ initially to gather usage and cost telemetry
Routing should favor Dedicated capacity first; fall back to Hosted with circuit-breaker if Dedicated not available
risks: High cost exposure if multiple rescues coincide with peak traffic windows
On-prem/resident data rescues require Legal sign-off per customer; may slow acceptance
Engineering capacity for urgent fixes could interfere with roadmap if not tightly timeboxed
Ambiguous acceptance criteria may lead to disputes with customers — must be explicit and contract-linked
